scenes.heading: Capacity and mass
scenes.sub: How much does it hold? How heavy is it?
scenes.say: How many litres does a fish tank hold? How heavy is a bag of rice? Let's learn the units for capacity and mass, and a neat link between volume and litres.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: How much water you can pour into a lunch box
scenes.science: Capacity: every 1 cm³ of space holds 1 mL
scenes.breaks: Real containers have thick walls, so the space inside is a bit less than the whole box.
scenes.say: Picture an empty lunch box. Its capacity is how much water you could pour into it. Every cubic centimetre of space inside holds exactly one millilitre of water.
scenes.caption: Picture an empty lunch box. Its capacity is how much water you could pour into it. Every 1 cm³ of space inside holds exactly 1 mL.

scenes.heading: Units to know
scenes.say: Capacity is measured in millilitres, litres and kilolitres. One litre is one thousand millilitres. Mass is measured in milligrams, grams, kilograms and tonnes. Notice that every jump between these units is one thousand.
scenes.caption: Capacity: mL, L, kL. 1 L = 1000 mL and 1 kL = 1000 L. Mass: mg, g, kg, t. Every jump between these units is 1000.

scenes.heading: Volume to capacity
steps: For water: 1 mL has a mass of 1 g
scenes.say: Here's how volume links to capacity. One cubic centimetre holds one millilitre. One thousand cubic centimetres holds one litre. One cubic metre holds one thousand litres. And for water only, one millilitre has a mass of one gram.
scenes.caption: 1 cm³ holds 1 mL. 1000 cm³ holds 1 L. 1 m³ holds 1000 L. For water only, 1 mL has a mass of 1 g.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: A container is 20 cm long, 10 cm wide and 15 cm high. How many litres does it hold?
scenes.say: A container is twenty centimetres long, ten wide and fifteen high. Its volume is three thousand cubic centimetres, so it holds three thousand millilitres. Divide by one thousand: three litres.
scenes.caption: A container 20 cm by 10 cm by 15 cm. Volume = 3000 cm³, so it holds 3000 mL. ÷ 1000: 3 L.

scenes.heading: Mass in kilograms
scenes.question: 24 cans of soup each have a mass of 375 g. Find the total mass in kg.
scenes.say: Twenty-four cans of soup each have a mass of three hundred and seventy-five grams. Multiply to get nine thousand grams. Divide by one thousand to change to kilograms: nine kilograms.
scenes.caption: 24 cans of 375 g. 24 × 375 = 9000 g. ÷ 1000: 9 kg.

scenes.say: Quick recap. A litre is one thousand millilitres, and a kilogram is one thousand grams. One cubic centimetre holds one millilitre, and one cubic metre holds one thousand litres. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. 1 L = 1000 mL and 1 kg = 1000 g. 1 cm³ holds 1 mL, and 1 m³ holds 1000 L. Now try the practice questions!
